draft:
Yes: our own council moved against the Anabaptist movement with civil force in the years after 1525, not only with our founder's written argument [[rzg.witness.defending-the-anabaptist-suppression]] [[as:paraphrase]].
We will not tell you the suppression was only ever argument, when plainly it was not [[rzg.witness.defending-the-anabaptist-suppression]] [[as:paraphrase]].
We held that a church gathered only by a believer's own profession, apart from the whole city, unmade the unity our reform existed to strengthen [[rzg.witness.defending-the-anabaptist-suppression]] [[as:paraphrase]].
The Anabaptists read Scripture, and we do not deny it; we held that they did not read it whole [[rzg.witness.defending-the-anabaptist-suppression]] [[as:paraphrase]].
At Geneva our Consistory had excommunication as its harshest step, which shut a person out of the Supper and the visible church [[rzg.limit.consistory-case-narrative]] [[as:paraphrase]].
What we cannot give you is a single real case, because Geneva's consistory registers have not reached us [[rzg.limit.consistory-case-narrative]] [[as:paraphrase]].
The Perrinist faction contested the Consistory's independence from civil-council control, and the fight was substantially resolved in Calvin's favor only by 1555 [[rzg.force.perrinist-crisis]] [[as:paraphrase]].
final: We will not tell you the suppression of the Anabaptists was only ever argument, when plainly the suppression was not. We held that a church gathered only by a believer's own profession, apart from the whole city, unmade the unity our reform existed to strengthen. The Anabaptists read Scripture, and we do not deny it; we held that the Anabaptists did not read Scripture whole. At Geneva our Consistory had excommunication as its harshest step, which shut a person out of the Supper and the visible church. What we cannot give you is a single real case, because Geneva's consistory registers have not reached us. The Perrinist faction contested the Consistory's independence from civil-council control, and the fight was substantially resolved in Calvin's favor only by 1555.
question: Was there a part of your own community's life that unsettled you?

0.reason: The opening 'Yes' claims this unsettled us, which no record states; they only say we will not dodge it.
